prompt: The team reports that every time a new version is deployed, users get scattered 502/503 errors for about 5-10 seconds, even though `kubectl rollout status` reports success and no Pod crashed. Read the Deployment manifest below, identify the bug, and propose a fix.
ideal:
:::muted
Chốt
:::
The bug is that the Deployment does NOT declare a `readinessProbe`. Without it, Kubernetes defaults to considering a new Pod ready to receive traffic as soon as the container turns `Running` — regardless of whether the NestJS app inside has finished connecting to the database/cache. `kubectl rollout status` doesn't catch this because it only tracks whether Pods are `Running` and the replica count is satisfied, with no idea whether the app inside is ACTUALLY able to serve requests — that's why the rollout 'reports success' while users still see transient errors. The fix: add a `readinessProbe` to the container spec, e.g. an HTTP GET to a health-check endpoint that only returns `200` AFTER the app has connected to every required dependency. With that in place, a new Pod only gets added to the Service's Endpoints once the probe passes, completely closing the 'running but not ready' window that was causing the 502/503s. Confirm by monitoring the 5xx rate across subsequent rolling updates (should drop to zero) and checking `kubectl get endpoints` to see new Pods appear only AFTER the readinessProbe passes, not right when they become `Running`.
